member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayerX.MediaPlayerCoreX
member.summary: MediaPlayerX audio effects processing implementation. This partial class provides comprehensive audio effects management including equalizers, filters, dynamic range control, spatial processing, and real-time audio manipulation during media playback. Supports both GStreamer-based and platform-specific audio processing pipelines.

MediaPlayerX bus message handling and pipeline event processing implementation. This partial class manages the communication between the MediaBlocks pipeline and the MediaPlayerX, handling pipeline state changes, stream information updates, error events, and other bus messages to provide a cohesive media player experience with proper event forwarding and state management.

MediaPlayerX callback and event handling implementation. This partial class manages all callback functions and event handlers for media processing events, including audio/video frame callbacks, pipeline events, error handling, and user interaction events. Provides the bridge between low-level MediaBlocks events and high-level MediaPlayerX events.

MediaPlayerX core initialization and pipeline management implementation. This partial class handles the fundamental setup and configuration of the MediaBlocks pipeline, including source block initialization, audio/video renderer setup, effects chain configuration, and core event handling for the media player functionality.

MediaPlayerX license validation and feature requirement checking implementation. This partial class handles license level validation and feature restriction enforcement based on the current license tier, checking for professional features and triggering appropriate license requirement events when insufficient license levels are detected.

MediaPlayerX logging and context management implementation. This partial class provides access to the underlying logging infrastructure and context used by the MediaBlocks pipeline, enabling centralized logging and debugging capabilities for the MediaPlayerX component.

Cross-platform Media Player SDK core class that provides comprehensive media playback capabilities. This class serves as the main entry point for media playback functionality, supporting various media sources (files, streams, cameras), multiple output formats, real-time effects processing, and cross-platform rendering. Built on the MediaBlocks pipeline system and GStreamer for maximum compatibility and performance.

MediaPlayerX configurable properties and settings implementation. This partial class contains all properties for controlling media playback behavior, effects processing, audio/video configuration, and advanced features like subtitle handling, stream selection, and hardware acceleration. Provides comprehensive control over the MediaPlayerX functionality through bindable properties.

MediaPlayerX metadata and tag reading implementation. This partial class provides comprehensive media file metadata extraction capabilities including ID3 tags, album art, artist information, and technical metadata from various media formats. Supports MP4, MP3, OGG, WMV, and other common media container formats.

MediaPlayerX video composition and layering implementation. This partial class provides advanced video composition capabilities including multi-layer video mixing, overlay management, picture-in-picture effects, and real-time video compositing during playback. Supports dynamic addition and manipulation of composition elements without interrupting playback.

MediaPlayerX video effects processing implementation. This partial class provides comprehensive video effects management including filters, color correction, geometric transformations, artistic effects, and real-time video manipulation during media playback. Supports dynamic effect addition, removal, and parameter adjustment without interrupting playback.

MediaPlayerX video processing and computer vision implementation. This partial class provides advanced video processing capabilities including motion detection, frame analysis, computer vision algorithms, and real-time video processing during playback. Integrates with AForge.NET and other computer vision libraries for advanced video analysis.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayerX.MediaPlayerCoreX.NextFrame
member.summary: Advances the video playback by exactly one frame (frame stepping forward). This method pauses the player and moves forward by a single frame, useful for precise video analysis or frame-by-frame examination. The operation requires a video renderer to be present and only works with seekable sources like media files, not live streams.
member.returns: true if the frame step operation was successful; false if it failed due to missing video renderer or unsupported source.
member.remarks: Frame stepping behavior: - Automatically pauses playback before stepping to ensure precise control - Handles negative playback rates by switching to positive rate during the step - Requires a video renderer to be configured in the player - Only works with seekable media sources (files), not live streams - The step size respects the current playback rate for timing calculations Use this method for precise video analysis, educational content, or debugging purposes.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayerX.MediaPlayerCoreX.PrevFrame
member.summary: Steps backward by exactly one frame (reverse frame stepping). This method moves the playback position backward by a single frame using seek operations, useful for precise video analysis in reverse. The operation requires seekable video content and may be slower than forward frame stepping due to the need for precise backward seeking.
member.returns: true if the backward frame step was successful; false if it failed due to missing pipeline, no video streams, or seek limitations.
member.remarks: Backward frame stepping limitations and behavior: - Requires a valid pipeline and at least one video stream - Only works with seekable media sources (files), not live streams - Uses seek operations which may be slower than forward stepping - Accuracy depends on the underlying codec's ability to seek to exact frames - May not work reliably with all video formats or codecs - Performance varies based on video compression and keyframe intervals This method is primarily intended for video analysis and educational purposes where precise backward navigation is needed.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayerX.MediaPlayerCoreX.Audio_Stream_Select(VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.AudioStreamInfo)
member.summary: Switches to a different audio stream in multi-stream media content. This method allows dynamic switching between audio tracks during playback, commonly used for multi-language content or content with multiple audio channels (commentary, music, etc.). The switch occurs seamlessly without interrupting video playback.
member.param: The target audio stream to switch to. Must be a valid from the media's available audio streams.
member.returns: true if the audio stream was successfully switched; false if the operation failed due to invalid source, null stream, or GStreamer event failure.
member.remarks: Audio stream switching behavior: - Maintains current video stream while switching audio - Sends a SELECT_STREAMS event to the underlying GStreamer pipeline - Works during active playback without interruption - Requires the media to contain multiple audio streams - The target stream must be available in the current media content Use this method for implementing audio track selection in media players with multi-language or multi-channel content.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.ONVIFDiscovery.Interfaces.IDiscovery
member.summary: Provides functionality to discover ONVIF compliant devices on the network using the WS-Discovery protocol.
member.remarks: This interface defines methods for discovering ONVIF devices through multicast UDP probes. Implementations should handle network communication and parse discovery responses according to the ONVIF specification.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.ONVIFDiscovery.Interfaces.IDiscovery.Discover(System.Int32,System.Action{VisioForge.Core.ONVIFDiscovery.Models.DiscoveryDevice},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Discovers ONVIF devices on the network and invokes a callback for each device found.
member.param: The maximum time in seconds to wait for device responses before completing the discovery process.
A callback action that is invoked for each discovered device as responses are received.
An optional cancellation token to cancel the discovery operation.
member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous discovery operation.
member.remarks: This method provides real-time notifications as devices are discovered, making it suitable for UI scenarios where you want to display devices as they are found rather than waiting for all devices to respond.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.ONVIFDiscovery.Interfaces.IDiscovery.Discover(System.Int32,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Discovers all ONVIF devices on the network and returns them as a collection.
member.param: The maximum time in seconds to wait for device responses before completing the discovery process.
An optional cancellation token to cancel the discovery operation.
member.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation, containing a collection of discovered instances.
member.remarks: This method waits for the specified timeout period to collect all device responses before returning. Use the overload if you need real-time notifications as devices are discovered.

member.summary: Provides an abstraction over UDP client functionality for ONVIF device discovery.
member.remarks: This interface wraps the to enable easier testing and to provide ONVIF-specific functionality for sending discovery probes and receiving responses.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.ONVIFDiscovery.Interfaces.IUdpClientFactory
member.summary: Factory interface for creating instances for ONVIF device discovery.
member.remarks: This factory pattern allows for flexible creation of UDP clients, supporting both single endpoint scenarios and multi-interface discovery where clients are created for each available network interface.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.ONVIFDiscovery.Interfaces.IUdpClientFactory.CreateClient(System.Net.IPEndPoint)
member.summary: Creates an configured for the specified endpoint.
member.param: The local endpoint to bind the UDP client to, determining which network interface and port to use.
member.returns: A new instance of bound to the specified endpoint.
member.remarks: The endpoint parameter typically specifies a local IP address and port. For ONVIF discovery, this is often a specific network interface address with port 0 (any available port).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.ONVIFDiscovery.Interfaces.IUdpClientFactory.CreateClientForeachInterface
member.summary: Creates UDP clients for all available network interfaces to enable comprehensive device discovery.
member.returns: A collection of instances, one for each valid network interface.
member.remarks: This method is useful for discovering devices across all network segments when a system has multiple network interfaces. It typically excludes loopback interfaces and creates clients only for active, up interfaces that support IPv4. Each client can independently send and receive discovery messages on its respective network interface.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.ONVIFDiscovery.Models.DiscoveryDevice
member.summary: Represents an ONVIF-compliant device discovered on the network through WS-Discovery.
member.remarks: This class contains all the information received from a device's probe response during the discovery process, including service endpoints, device metadata, and capability information encoded in scopes.

member.value: A collection of type identifiers such as "NetworkVideoTransmitter" for cameras, "NetworkVideoDisplay" for displays, or "NetworkVideoAnalytics" for analytics devices.
member.remarks: These types follow the ONVIF device type naming convention and indicate what kind of services and capabilities the device supports.

member.remarks: These addresses (XAddrs in WS-Discovery terminology) are the entry points for accessing the device's ONVIF services. Multiple addresses may be provided if the device is accessible through different network interfaces or protocols.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.ONVIFDiscovery.Models.DiscoveryDevice.Model

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.ONVIFDiscovery.Models.DiscoveryDevice.Address

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.ONVIFDiscovery.Models.DiscoveryDevice.Scopes

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.SimplePlayerX.SimplePlayerCoreX
member.summary: Provides GStreamer bus message handling for SimplePlayerX, managing PlayBin3 pipeline events and state changes. This partial class handles asynchronous communication from the GStreamer pipeline including video overlay setup, stream collection parsing, error propagation, end-of-stream notifications, and state transition monitoring. Essential for maintaining player state and providing event notifications in the simplified player implementation. Implements the . Implements the .

Provides comprehensive logging and telemetry functionality for SimplePlayerX using Serilog and Sentry. This partial class manages structured logging to files and debug output, error event propagation, and optional telemetry collection during development. Configures logging levels, file rotation, pipeline debugging, and integrates with Sentry for crash reporting and debugging support in simple media player operations. Implements the . Implements the .

Provides a simplified, cross-platform media player implementation using GStreamer's PlayBin3 for easy media playback. This class offers a streamlined interface for basic media playback operations including play, pause, stop, seek, and volume control. Built on top of GStreamer's high-level PlayBin3 element, it automatically handles codec discovery, format negotiation, and pipeline construction. Supports multiple stream types (video, audio, subtitles), stream switching, and provides comprehensive error handling and logging capabilities. Implements the . Implements the .

Provides stream management and selection functionality for SimplePlayerX, handling multiple audio, video, and subtitle streams within media content. This partial class manages stream discovery, enumeration, and dynamic stream switching during playback using GStreamer's stream selection events. Essential for handling multi-stream media files and providing user control over active streams in the player. Implements the . Implements the .

member.summary: Defines a collection of preset environments for the I3DL2 (Interactive 3D Audio Rendering Guidelines Level 2.0) reverb effect. These presets simulate the acoustic properties of various physical spaces.
member.remarks: I3DL2 reverb is used to add spatial realism to audio by simulating reflections and echoes within a virtual environment. Each preset configures parameters like decay time, early reflections, and late reverberation to mimic a specific type of room or space.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat
member.summary: Defines the audio format for raw audio data, specifying whether it is Pulse-Code Modulation (PCM), IEEE floating-point, or encoded. This enumeration is crucial for configuring audio streams and ensuring correct data interpretation throughout the framework.
member.remarks: Use this enumeration to specify the sample format for audio capture, processing, and playback. For example, when setting up an audio source, you would select a member of this enum to define the expected audio data format.

example.code: // To configure an audio source to use 16-bit PCM audio: var audioFormat = AudioFormat.PCM16;

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.PCM8
member.summary: 8-bit unsigned integer Pulse-Code Modulation (PCM) format. This format provides a basic level of audio quality.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.PCM16
member.summary: 16-bit signed integer PCM format. This is a standard format for CD-quality audio.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.PCM24
member.summary: 24-bit signed integer PCM format. Used in professional audio for higher dynamic range.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.PCM32
member.summary: 32-bit signed integer PCM format. Offers even greater precision than 24-bit PCM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.IEEE32
member.summary: 32-bit floating-point (IEEE 754) format. Commonly used in audio processing to prevent clipping and preserve quality during intermediate calculations.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.Unknown
member.summary: Represents an unknown or unspecified audio format. This value is typically used as a default or to indicate an error state.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.IEEE64
member.summary: 64-bit double-precision floating-point (IEEE 754) format. Provides the highest level of precision for audio processing, though it is less common and more resource-intensive.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.Encoded
member.summary: Indicates that the audio data is in a compressed or encoded format (e.g., MP3, AAC), rather than raw PCM samples.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.GIFResizeStretchMode
member.summary: Defines how a GIF frame should be resized or stretched to fit a target dimension.
member.remarks: This enumeration is used to control the aspect ratio and scaling behavior when creating GIFs from source video frames that may have a different size.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.GIFResizeStretchMode.Stretch
member.summary: Stretches the frame to fill the target dimensions completely, which may distort the original aspect ratio.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.GIFResizeStretchMode.Letterbox
member.summary: Resizes the frame to fit within the target dimensions while maintaining the original aspect ratio. Black bars (letterboxing) will be added to fill any empty space if the aspect ratios do not match.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.GIFResizeStretchMode.Crop
member.summary: Resizes the frame to fill the target dimensions while maintaining the original aspect ratio. The frame will be cropped if its aspect ratio does not match the target, ensuring no black bars are present.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.GIFResizeStretchMode.None
member.summary: The frame is not resized. It will be centered in the output, and if it is larger than the target dimensions, it will be cropped. If it is smaller, the surrounding area will be filled with a background color.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IBitmap
member.summary: Represents a platform-agnostic bitmap image. This interface is used as a common wrapper for different bitmap implementations across various platforms (e.g., Windows, Android, iOS).
member.remarks: The primary purpose of this interface is to allow for the manipulation and passing of bitmap images in a generic way, without coupling the core logic to a specific UI framework or image library. Implementations of this interface are expected to handle the platform-specific details of bitmap creation, manipulation, and disposal. As it implements , instances should be properly disposed of to release underlying resources.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IMediaPlayerControls
member.summary: Defines a standard set of controls for a media player component. This interface provides a common API for controlling playback of media files, including play, pause, stop, seek, and volume adjustments. It also includes asynchronous versions of most methods for use in responsive UI applications.
member.remarks: This interface inherits from , providing access to video effect adjustments in addition to playback controls. Implementations of this interface are expected to manage the underlying media playback engine.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.IMediaPlayerControls.Play(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Starts or preloads the media for playback.
member.param: If set to true, the media is loaded and ready to play but does not start automatically.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IVideoViewNativeRendering
member.summary: Defines an interface for video view components that support switching to a native rendering backend. This is typically used to improve performance in demanding scenarios, such as playing high-resolution (4K/8K) video or using hardware-accelerated GPU decoding.
member.remarks: When native rendering is enabled, the video is rendered directly by the underlying system's graphics API (e.g., DirectX, OpenGL) instead of through a higher-level UI framework like WPF. This can significantly reduce CPU usage and improve rendering smoothness, but may have implications for UI integration and layering.

member.summary: Enables or disables native rendering for the video view.
member.param: Set to true to enable native rendering; false to use the default framework rendering (e.g., WPF).
member.remarks: It is recommended to enable this for performance-critical applications, such as those involving GPU-accelerated decoding or ultra-high-definition video.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IVideoViewPushFrame
member.summary: Defines an interface for video views that support direct pushing of video frames for rendering. This interface is crucial for scenarios where raw video data needs to be displayed without relying on a traditional media pipeline (e.g., for custom video processing or real-time frame injection).
member.remarks: Implementations of this interface are responsible for taking raw video frame data and rendering it efficiently to the display. This allows for fine-grained control over the video rendering process.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags
member.summary: Represents a comprehensive collection of metadata tags for a media file. This class aggregates various pieces of information commonly found in audio and video file tags (e.g., ID3, MP4 tags).
member.remarks: This class is designed to provide a unified access point to media file metadata, regardless of the underlying tag format. It includes standard fields like title, artist, album, and genre, as well as more specific fields like MusicBrainz IDs and ReplayGain information.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.TagTypes
member.summary: Gets or sets the types of tags contained in the current instance, represented as a bitwise combined enumeration. This indicates which tag formats (e.g., ID3v1, ID3v2, APE) are present in the media file.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Title
member.summary: Gets or sets the title of the media described by the current instance. This is most commonly the name of a song, episode, or movie title.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Performers
member.summary: Gets or sets the performers or artists who performed in the media described by the current instance.
member.value: A array containing the performers or artists, or an empty array if no value is present.
member.remarks: This field is commonly called "Artists" in media applications and should represent each of the artists appearing in the media.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.AlbumArtists
member.summary: Gets or sets the band or artist credited for the entire album or collection containing the media.
member.value: A array containing the album artists, or an empty array if no value is present.
member.remarks: This field is typically optional but aids in the sorting of compilations or albums with multiple artists.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Composers
member.summary: Gets or sets the composers of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A array containing the composers, or an empty array if no value is present.
member.remarks: This field represents the composers, songwriters, scriptwriters, or persons who claim authorship of the media.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Album
member.summary: Gets or sets the album of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A object containing the album name, or if no value is present.
member.remarks: This field represents the name of the album the media belongs to. For boxed sets, it should be the name of the entire set.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Comment
member.summary: Gets or sets a user comment on the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A object containing user comments, or if no value is present.
member.remarks: This field should be used to store user notes and comments. It should not contain program information.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Subtitle
member.summary: Gets or sets the subtitle tag for the media.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Genres

member.value: A array containing the genres, or an empty array if no value is present.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Year
member.summary: Gets or sets the year that the media represented by the current instance was recorded or released.
member.value: A containing the year, or zero if no value is present.
member.remarks: Years greater than 9999 cannot be stored by most tagging formats. Some formats support higher precision dates.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Track
member.summary: Gets or sets the position of the media represented by the current instance in its containing album.
member.value: A containing the track number, or zero if not specified.
member.remarks: This value should be the same as is listed on the album cover and no more than if is non-zero.

member.value: A containing the total track count, or zero if not specified.

member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz Disc ID, or an empty array if no value is present.
member.remarks: This field represents the MusicBrainz Disc ID, and is used to uniquely identify the particular Released Media associated with this track.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicIpId
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicIP PUID of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicIP PUID, or an empty array if no value is present.
member.remarks: This field represents the MusicIP PUID, and is an acoustic fingerprint identifier. It Identifies what this track "Sounds Like".

member.summary: Gets or sets the Amazon ID of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the Amazon ID, or an empty array if no value is present.
member.remarks: This field represents the Amazon ID, and is used to identify the particular track or album in the Amazon Catalog.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicBrainz_ReleaseStatus
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicBrainz Release Status of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz Release Status, or an empty array if no value is present.
member.remarks: This field represents the MusicBrainz Release Status, and is used to describes how 'official' a Release is. Common Status are: Official, Promotion, Bootleg, Pseudo-release.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicBrainz_ReleaseType
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicBrainz Release Type of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz Release Type, or an empty array if no value is present.
member.remarks: This field represents the MusicBrainz Release Type, that describes what kind of release a Release is. Common Status are: Single, Album, EP, Compilation, Soundtrack, SpokenWord, Interview, Audiobook, Live, Remix, and Other. Careful thought must be given when using this field to decide if a particular track "Is a Compilation".

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicBrainz_ReleaseCountry
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicBrainz Release Country of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz Release Country, or an empty array if no value is present.
member.remarks: This field represents the MusicBrainz Release Country, that describes the country in which an album was released. Note that the Release Country of an album is not necessarily the country in which it was produced. The label itself will typically be more relevant. eg, a release on "Foo Records UK" that has "Made in Austria" printed on it, will likely be a UK release.

member.summary: Specifies the types of barcodes that can be recognized or generated by the video processing components. This enumeration includes various 1D (linear) and 2D (matrix) barcode formats.
member.remarks: When configuring a barcode reader, selecting the appropriate barcode type can improve detection accuracy and performance. The option attempts to detect all supported types but may be slower.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.CamshiftMode
member.summary: Specifies the color space mode to be used by the Camshift (Continuously Adaptive Mean-Shift) tracking algorithm. The choice of color space can significantly impact the robustness and accuracy of object tracking.
member.remarks: Camshift is an algorithm for tracking non-rigid objects. It relies on a color histogram of the target object. Different color spaces offer varying degrees of robustness to changes in lighting and object orientation.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.CamshiftMode.RGB
member.summary: The tracker will process raw high-intensity RGB (Red, Green, Blue) values. This mode is sensitive to lighting changes but can be effective for objects with distinct color signatures.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.CamshiftMode.HSL
member.summary: The tracker will perform an RGB-to-HSL (Hue, Saturation, Lightness) conversion and primarily use the Hue component. This mode is generally more robust to changes in lighting conditions.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.CamshiftMode.Mixed
member.summary: The tracker will use a combination of HSL with some lightness information. This mode attempts to balance color robustness with some intensity information.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.FaceTrackingSettings
member.summary: Represents the settings for configuring face tracking operations within the video processing components. This class allows control over parameters such as minimum face size, color mode, search mode, and scaling factors.
member.remarks: Proper configuration of these settings is crucial for optimizing face detection and tracking performance and accuracy for various scenarios, such as different camera distances, lighting conditions, or target face sizes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.FaceTrackingSettings.MinimumWindowSize
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum window size (in pixels) to consider when searching for objects (faces). Objects smaller than this size will be ignored. Default value is 25.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.FaceTrackingSettings.ColorMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the color mode to be used by the face tracking algorithm.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.FaceTrackingSettings.SearchMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the search mode for face tracking, determining whether to detect a single face or multiple faces.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.FaceTrackingSettings.ScaleFactor
member.summary: Gets or sets the scaling factor used to rescale the search window during the detection process. A smaller value (e.g., 1.05) means a finer search, potentially more accurate but slower. Default value is 1.2f.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.FaceTrackingSettings.ScalingMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the scaling mode to use when re-scaling the search window during detection. Default is .

member.summary: Defines the contract for a face detection component. This interface extends , indicating that face detection is a form of video processing.
member.remarks: Implementations of this interface are responsible for analyzing video frames to identify human faces. The results of the detection are communicated through the event.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.IFaceDetector.FacesDetected
member.summary: Occurs when one or more faces are detected in a video frame. The event provides a object containing details about the detected faces.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.IVideoProcessor
member.summary: Defines the contract for a video processing component. This interface provides methods for processing individual video frames and querying supported formats.
member.remarks: Implementations of this interface can perform various video manipulations, such as applying effects, analyzing content, or transforming frames. It supports processing both legacy and modern types.

member.summary: Processes a video frame of type . This method is typically used for processing frames from the MediaBlocks engine.

member.summary: Processes a video frame of type . This method is typically used for processing frames from legacy video sources.

member.returns: An array of supported video formats.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.IVideoProcessor.SetContext(VisioForge.Core.BaseContext)
member.summary: Sets the operational context for the video processor. This can be used to provide necessary dependencies or shared resources to the processor.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorScalingMode
member.summary: Specifies the scaling strategy for the search window used in object detection algorithms. This mode determines how the detector iterates through different sizes of objects to find matches.
member.remarks: The choice of scaling mode can impact both the performance and accuracy of object detection. For example, if you expect to detect large objects primarily, starting with larger windows might be more efficient.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorScalingMode.GreaterToSmaller
member.summary: The object detector will start searching with larger windows and gradually scale down to smaller ones. This mode can be efficient if the target objects are expected to be large.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorScalingMode.SmallerToGreater
member.summary: The object detector will start searching with smaller windows and gradually scale up to larger ones. This mode can be efficient if the target objects are expected to be small.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorSearchMode
member.summary: Specifies the search mode for object detection algorithms. This enumeration defines how the detector scans an image or video frame for objects.
member.remarks: The choice of search mode can significantly affect the performance and the number of detected objects. For example, mode is faster if only one object is expected, while (full scan) is more comprehensive.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorSearchMode.Default
member.summary: The entire image or video frame will be scanned for objects. This is the default and most comprehensive search mode.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorSearchMode.Single
member.summary: Only a single object will be retrieved. The search stops after the first object is found. This mode is useful for performance optimization when only the presence of an object matters.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorSearchMode.NoOverlap
member.summary: If an object has already been detected within an area, that area will not be scanned again for inner or overlapping objects. This can save computation time and prevent redundant detections.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorSearchMode.Average
member.summary: If several objects are located within one another (overlapping detections), their bounding boxes will be averaged into a single result. This helps in consolidating multiple detections of the same object.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode
member.summary: Specifies the deinterlacing modes available for the Enhanced Video Renderer (EVR). Deinterlacing converts interlaced video (where each frame consists of two fields captured at different times) into progressive video (where each frame contains all lines of a single moment in time).
member.remarks: Proper deinterlacing is crucial for displaying interlaced content (e.g., from broadcast TV, DVDs) on progressive displays (e.g., computer monitors, LCD TVs) without artifacts like combing. The choice of mode can impact visual quality and CPU/GPU usage.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode.Auto
member.summary: The EVR automatically selects the best deinterlacing method based on the video content and available hardware capabilities. This is generally the recommended setting for optimal quality and performance.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode.ForceHalfInterlace
member.summary: Forces the EVR to skip the second field (in temporal order) of every interlaced frame. This results in half-resolution video but can be useful for very low-latency scenarios or when higher-quality deinterlacing is not needed or causes performance issues.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode.ForceBob
member.summary: Forces the EVR to use bob deinterlacing. Bob deinterlacing creates a full frame from each field by interpolating missing lines, resulting in smoother motion but potentially visible artifacts.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode.AllowDropToHalfInterlace
member.summary: Allows the EVR to drop to half-interlace mode if it is falling behind in rendering. This provides a fallback for performance, sacrificing quality for smoothness.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode.AllowDropToBob
member.summary: Allows the EVR to drop to bob deinterlacing if it is falling behind in rendering. This provides a fallback for performance, sacrificing some quality for smoother playback.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode
member.summary: Specifies the video rendering engine to be used for displaying video frames. The choice of renderer can impact performance, compatibility, and available features.
member.remarks: Different rendering modes are optimized for various platforms and scenarios. Some renderers are specific to Windows (WinForms, WPF, WinUI) while others might be more generic or callback-based.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode.VideoRenderer
member.summary: The legacy Video Renderer, primarily available for WinForms applications. This renderer is deprecated and generally not recommended for new development.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode.VMR9
member.summary: Video Mixing Renderer 9, available for WinForms applications. Offers improved video mixing capabilities compared to the legacy Video Renderer.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode.EVR
member.summary: Enhanced Video Renderer (EVR), available on Windows Vista and later. This is a modern renderer offering better performance and quality, especially with hardware acceleration. Available for WinForms applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode.None
member.summary: No video renderer is used. This might be chosen when only audio processing or file saving is required, or when a custom rendering solution is implemented.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode.WPF_WinUI_Callback
member.summary: A rendering mode suitable for WPF, WinUI, or custom callback-based rendering scenarios. This mode typically involves receiving video frames as callbacks for manual rendering.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode.WPF_NativeHWND
member.summary: A rendering mode for WPF applications that uses a native HWND (window handle) for rendering. This can offer better performance and compatibility with certain video sources or effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode.Direct2D
member.summary: Direct2D renderer, offering high-performance 2D graphics rendering. Available for both WinForms and WPF applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode.Direct2DManaged
member.summary: A managed Direct2D renderer, specifically designed for WPF applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode.MadVR
member.summary: madVR renderer, a high-quality video renderer known for its advanced scaling and rendering algorithms. Primarily available for WinForms applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode.WinUI
member.summary: The WinUI 3 renderer, designed for applications built with the WinUI 3 framework.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererMode.FrameCallback
member.summary: An alias for , indicating a mode where video frames are delivered via callbacks for custom rendering.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererStretchMode
member.summary: Specifies how video frames are scaled or stretched to fit the display area of a video renderer. This enumeration controls the aspect ratio preservation and filling behavior.
member.remarks: The choice of stretch mode affects how the video appears when its aspect ratio differs from the display area. Some modes preserve the aspect ratio by adding black bars, while others stretch the video to fill the entire area, potentially causing distortion.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererStretchMode.Letterbox
member.summary: Preserves the video's original aspect ratio by adding black bars (letterboxing or pillarboxing) to fill any empty space in the display area.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererStretchMode.Stretch
member.summary: Stretches the video to fill the entire display area, ignoring its original aspect ratio. This may result in a distorted image if the aspect ratios do not match.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererStretchMode.LetterboxToFill
member.summary: Stretches the video to fill the entire display area while preserving its aspect ratio. This is achieved by cropping the video if its aspect ratio does not match the display area. This mode is typically available for WPF renderers.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoStreamType
member.summary: Defines the type of a video stream, typically used in frame grabber events or when managing multiple video sources. This enumeration helps distinguish between main video, preview, capture, and Picture-in-Picture (PIP) streams.
member.remarks: When working with video processing or display, identifying the stream type is essential for applying correct logic, such as routing frames to different renderers or applying specific effects.

member.remarks: The choice of UI engine impacts how video is displayed and integrated into an application's user interface. Some engines are platform-specific (e.g., WinForms, Android), while others offer cross-platform capabilities (e.g., Avalonia, MAUI).

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for barcode detection events within the VisioForge X engine. This class encapsulates information about the detected barcode, including its type, value, and the timestamp of detection.
member.remarks: This event argument is used when a barcode is successfully identified in a video frame or image processed by the X engine. It allows applications to react to barcode detections, such as logging the information, triggering actions, or displaying results.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorEventArgs.BarcodeType
member.summary: Gets the type of the detected barcode (e.g., "QR_CODE", "EAN_13", "CODE_39").

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorEventArgs.Value
member.summary: Gets the decoded string value of the barcode.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorEventArgs.Timestamp
member.summary: Gets the timestamp of the video frame or image at which the barcode was detected.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorEventArgs.#ctor(System.String,System.String,System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.param: The type of the detected barcode.
The decoded string value of the barcode.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorMode
member.summary: Specifies the operational mode for a barcode detector within the VisioForge X engine. This enumeration defines how the barcode detector interacts with the video processing pipeline.
member.remarks: The choice of mode depends on whether the original video stream needs to be passed through the detector or if only the detection results are required.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorMode.InputOnly
member.summary: In this mode, the barcode detector processes the input video stream but does not pass the video frames to its output. The output pad is effectively closed, meaning no video will be rendered or further processed after detection. This is useful when only the barcode detection results are needed, and the video stream itself is not required downstream.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorMode.InputOutput
member.summary: In this mode, the barcode detector processes the input video stream and then passes the original video frames to its output. This allows the video to be rendered or further processed by other components in the pipeline after barcode detection.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings
member.summary: Provides a set of debugging and control settings for media blocks within the VisioForge X engine. These settings allow for fine-grained control over buffer handling, timing, and error simulation for testing and diagnostic purposes.
member.remarks: This class is primarily intended for developers and advanced users to debug and analyze the behavior of media pipelines. Modifying these settings can significantly alter the performance and stability of media processing.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.CheckImperfectOffset
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to send element messages if buffer offsets and offset_ends do not match up. This helps in debugging issues related to buffer segmentation and continuity.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.CheckImperfectTimestamp
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to send element messages if buffer timestamps and durations do not match up. This helps in debugging issues related to timing and synchronization.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.DataRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the data rate in bytes per second for (re)timestamping buffers. If set to 0, this feature is inactive. Useful for simulating specific data flow rates.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.DropAllocation
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to drop allocation queries. If set to true, the element will not forward allocation queries, which can be used for testing memory management scenarios.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.DropProbability
member.summary: Gets or sets the probability (0.0 to 1.0) that a buffer will be dropped. This can be used to simulate network packet loss or other data corruption scenarios.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.EOSAfter
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of buffers after which an End-Of-Stream (EOS) signal will be sent. A value of -1 means no EOS will be sent based on buffer count. Useful for testing stream termination.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.ErrorAfter
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of buffers after which an error will be simulated. A value of -1 means no error will be simulated based on buffer count. Useful for testing error handling.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.SignalHandoffs
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the identity element should emit a handoff signal when processing a buffer. This signal can be used for external monitoring or debugging of buffer flow.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.Silent
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the media block should operate in silent mode. In silent mode, less debug information might be printed to the console.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.SingleSegment
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to timestamp buffers and eat segments so as to appear as one continuous segment. This is useful for ensuring continuous playback even with fragmented input.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.SleepTime
member.summary: Gets or sets the time in microseconds to sleep between processing each buffer. This can be used to simulate processing delays or to throttle the pipeline for debugging purposes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.Sync
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the media block should synchronize to the pipeline clock. Enabling synchronization ensures smooth playback and proper timing with other elements in the pipeline.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.TimestampOffset
member.summary: Gets or sets the timestamp offset in nanoseconds for synchronization. A negative value indicates an earlier synchronization point, while a positive value indicates a later one.

member.summary: Selects a trigger starting the capture of one frame.

member.summary: Selects a trigger controlling the duration of one frame (mainly used in line scan mode).

member.summary: Selects a trigger starting the capture of bursts of frames in an acquisition. Acquisition Burst Frame Count controls the length of each burst unless a Frame Burst End trigger is active. member.summary: Selects a trigger controlling the duration of the capture of the bursts of frames in an acquisition.

member.param: An object to compare with this instance.
member.returns:
A value that indicates the relative order of the objects being compared. The return value has these meanings: Value Meaning
Less than zero This instance precedes in the sort order.
Zero This instance occurs in the same position in the sort order as .
Greater than zero This instance follows in the sort order.

member.summary: Compares the current instance with another object of the same type and returns an integer that indicates whether the current instance precedes, follows, or occurs in the same position in the sort order as the other object. The comparison is based on the font family name.

A value that indicates the relative order of the objects being compared. Value Meaning
Less than zero This instance precedes in the sort order.
Zero This instance occurs in the same position in the sort order as .
Greater than zero This instance follows in the sort order.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IAudioVolumeMute

member.remarks: Implementations of this interface are typically found in audio processing elements or renderers within the MediaBlocks framework. It allows for programmatic control over the audio output.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IBaseSourceX
member.summary: Defines a base interface for media sources within the VisioForge X engine. This interface serves as a marker for all source elements in the MediaBlocks framework.
member.remarks: Implementations of this interface are responsible for providing media data (video, audio, etc.) to the processing pipeline. Specific source types (e.g., file sources, camera sources, network sources) will implement this interface along with more specialized interfaces.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IEncoderTextInfo
member.summary: Defines an interface for components that can provide textual information about encoder parameters and capabilities. This is useful for debugging, logging, or displaying detailed encoder settings to the user.
member.remarks: Implementations of this interface are typically found in encoder configuration classes within the MediaBlocks framework. It allows for a standardized way to retrieve human-readable descriptions of complex encoder settings.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IEncoderTextInfo.GetParameters
member.summary: Retrieves a string representation of the encoder's current parameters. This string typically includes settings like bitrate, resolution, frame rate, and other configured options.
member.returns: A containing the encoder parameters.

member.summary: Retrieves a string representation of the encoder's capabilities (GStreamer caps). This string describes the media formats and properties that the encoder can handle.
member.returns: A containing the encoder's capabilities.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IGetVideoStreamInfo
member.summary: Defines an interface for components that can provide detailed information about a video stream.
member.remarks: This interface is typically implemented by video sources or processing elements that can expose the properties of the video data they handle. It allows other parts of the system to query for video stream characteristics like resolution, frame rate, and codec.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IGetVideoStreamInfo.GetVideoStreamInfo
member.summary: Retrieves detailed information about the video stream.
member.returns: A object containing the video stream's properties.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IMediaBlocksPipelineCustomErrorHandler
member.summary: Defines an interface for custom error handling within a MediaBlocks pipeline. Implementations of this interface can intercept and process errors that occur during pipeline execution.
member.remarks: By implementing this interface and registering it with a MediaBlocks pipeline, developers can gain fine-grained control over how errors are managed. The method allows for custom logic to decide whether the pipeline should attempt to recover from an error or stop.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IMediaBlocksPipelineCustomErrorHandler.ErrorHandler(Gst.Bus,Gst.Message,Gst.Pipeline)
member.summary: Handles an error message received from the GStreamer bus.
member.param: The GStreamer bus that emitted the error message.
The GStreamer object containing the error details.
The GStreamer instance where the error occurred.
member.returns: true if the error was handled and the pipeline should attempt to continue working; false if the error was not handled or if the pipeline should stop.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX
member.summary: Specifies various pixel formats for images and video frames within the VisioForge X engine. This enumeration defines how color data is stored and interpreted for each pixel.
member.remarks: The choice of pixel format is crucial for correct rendering, processing, and compatibility with different hardware and software components. It includes common RGB, indexed, and alpha-channel formats.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Indexed
member.summary: The pixel data contains color-indexed values, meaning the values are an index to colors in the system color table, as opposed to individual color values.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Gdi
member.summary: The pixel data contains GDI (Graphics Device Interface) colors.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Alpha
member.summary: The pixel data contains alpha values that are not premultiplied.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.PAlpha
member.summary: The pixel format contains premultiplied alpha values.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Extended
member.summary: Reserved for future use or extended pixel formats.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Canonical
member.summary: The default pixel format of 32 bits per pixel. The format specifies 24-bit color depth and an 8-bit alpha channel.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Undefined
member.summary: The pixel format is undefined.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.DontCare
member.summary: No pixel format is specified. This value is typically used as a placeholder or when the format is not relevant.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format1bppIndexed
member.summary: Specifies that the pixel format is 1 bit per pixel and that it uses indexed color. The color table therefore has two colors in it.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format4bppIndexed
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 4 bits per pixel, indexed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format8bppIndexed
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 8 bits per pixel, indexed. The color table therefore has 256 colors in it.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppGrayScale
member.summary: The pixel format is 16 bits per pixel. The color information specifies 65536 shades of gray.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppRgb555
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 16 bits per pixel; 5 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components. The remaining bit is not used.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppRgb565
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 16 bits per pixel; 5 bits are used for the red component, 6 bits are used for the green component, and 5 bits are used for the blue component.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppArgb1555
member.summary: The pixel format is 16 bits per pixel. The color information specifies 32,768 shades of color, of which 5 bits are red, 5 bits are green, 5 bits are blue, and 1 bit is alpha.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format24bppRgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 24 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format32bppRgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 32 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components. The remaining 8 bits are not used.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format32bppArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 32 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format32bppPArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 32 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components. The red, green, and blue components are premultiplied, according to the alpha component.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format48bppRgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 48 bits per pixel; 16 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format64bppArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 64 bits per pixel; 16 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format64bppPArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 64 bits per pixel; 16 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components. The red, green, and blue components are premultiplied according to the alpha component.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Max
member.summary: The maximum value for this enumeration.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType
member.summary: Represents the media types supported in RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) payloads. This enumeration covers common audio and video codecs used in real-time streaming applications.
member.remarks: The RTP protocol is widely used for transmitting real-time data such as audio and video over IP networks. This enum helps in identifying the specific codec and format of the media being transported.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.H264
member.summary: H.264/AVC (Advanced Video Coding). Widely used video compression standard offering good quality and compression. Common in streaming, broadcasting, and video conferencing.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.H265
member.summary: H.265/HEVC (High Efficiency Video Coding). Next-generation video codec offering improved compression over H.264. Designed for 4K/8K resolutions and HDR content.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.VP8
member.summary: VP8 Video Codec. Open-source video codec developed by Google/WebM Project. Commonly used in WebRTC and web-based video applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.VP9
member.summary: VP9 Video Codec Successor to VP8, offering improved compression efficiency. Used extensively by YouTube and other web platforms.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.JPEG
member.summary: Motion JPEG. Series of JPEG images used for video compression. Commonly used in security cameras and professional video equipment.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.RAW
member.summary: Raw Video Format. Uncompressed video data in its native format. Used in professional video production and high-quality capture.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.AAC
member.summary: Advanced Audio Coding (AAC). Digital audio compression standard offering high quality at lower bitrates. Widely used in streaming services, digital broadcasting, and mobile devices.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.Opus
member.summary: Opus Audio Codec. Open-source, highly versatile audio codec. Excellent for both speech and music, with low latency for real-time applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.Vorbis
member.summary: Vorbis Audio Codec. Free and open-source audio compression format. Popular in game development and open-source multimedia applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.MP3
member.summary: MPEG Audio Layer III (MP3). Popular audio compression format with wide device support. Commonly used for music distribution and streaming.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.PCM
member.summary: Pulse Code Modulation (PCM). Raw digital representation of sampled analog signals. Used in professional audio equipment and high-quality recordings.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.G722
member.summary: G.722 Audio Codec. Wideband audio codec operating at 16 kHz sampling rate. Common in VoIP systems and digital telephony applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.AMR
member.summary: Adaptive Multi-Rate (AMR) Audio Codec. Speech codec optimized for voice communication. Widely used in GSM and UMTS mobile phone systems.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.Unknown
member.summary: The media type is unknown or not specified.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.AESCipher
member.summary: Specifies the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) cipher configuration.

remarks.para: AES is a symmetric encryption algorithm widely used for securing data. This enumeration defines the available AES key sizes and cipher modes.
Both options use CBC (Cipher Block Chaining) mode, which provides better security than ECB mode by making each cipher block dependent on all previous blocks.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.AESCipher.AES_128
member.summary: AES encryption with 128-bit key using CBC (Cipher Block Chaining) mode.

remarks.para: Provides strong encryption suitable for most applications. Uses a 128-bit (16 byte) key and requires a 128-bit initialization vector (IV).
Performance characteristics: Faster than AES-256 while still providing adequate security for most use cases.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.AESCipher.AES_256
member.summary: AES encryption with 256-bit key using CBC (Cipher Block Chaining) mode.

remarks.para: Provides the highest level of security with a 256-bit (32 byte) key. Requires a 128-bit initialization vector (IV) regardless of key size.
Recommended for highly sensitive data or when regulatory compliance requires maximum encryption strength.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings
member.summary: Provides configuration settings for AES encryption and decryption operations.

remarks.para: This class encapsulates all necessary parameters for AES encryption/decryption, including the cipher type, encryption key, initialization vector (IV), and IV serialization options.
The settings support both AES-128 and AES-256 encryption modes using CBC (Cipher Block Chaining).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings.Cipher
member.summary: Gets or sets the AES cipher configuration to use for encryption/decryption.
member.remarks: Determines the key size and encryption strength. AES-128 provides good security with better performance, while AES-256 offers maximum security.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings.Key
member.summary: Gets or sets the encryption key as a hexadecimal string.
member.value: The encryption key in hexadecimal format.

remarks.para: The key length must match the selected cipher: - AES-128: 32 hex characters (16 bytes) - AES-256: 64 hex characters (32 bytes)
Example: "0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF" for AES-128

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings.IV
member.summary: Gets or sets the initialization vector (IV) as a hexadecimal string.
member.value: The initialization vector in hexadecimal format. Must be 32 hex characters (16 bytes).

remarks.para: The IV is required for CBC mode and must be exactly 16 bytes (32 hex characters) regardless of the AES key size. Each encryption operation should use a unique IV for maximum security.
Example: "FEDCBA9876543210FEDCBA9876543210"

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings.SerializeIV
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the initialization vector (IV) should be serialized with the encrypted data.
member.value: true if the IV should be prepended to the encrypted data; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: When enabled, the IV is stored at the beginning of the encrypted output, allowing the decryption process to extract it automatically. This simplifies IV management but slightly increases the output size.
This is a common practice as the IV does not need to be kept secret, only unique for each encryption operation.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings.#ctor(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with the specified encryption key and initialization vector.
member.param: The encryption key as a hexadecimal string. Length must match the cipher requirements: 32 hex characters for AES-128, or 64 hex characters for AES-256.
The initialization vector as a hexadecimal string. Must be exactly 32 hex characters (16 bytes) for all AES cipher modes.
member.remarks: The constructor sets the default cipher to AES-128. Change the property after construction if AES-256 is required.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern
member.summary: Specifies the type of video test pattern to generate.

remarks.para: Test patterns are standardized video signals used for calibrating, testing, and troubleshooting video equipment and displays. They help verify proper signal transmission, color accuracy, and display geometry.
These patterns are commonly used in video editing applications as placeholders, for testing video pipelines, or as background elements.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Smpte
member.summary: SMPTE color bars test pattern.
member.remarks: The standard SMPTE (Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers) color bars pattern used for calibrating video equipment. Contains vertical bars of primary and secondary colors.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Snow
member.summary: Random noise pattern resembling analog TV static.
member.remarks: Generates a random black and white noise pattern, similar to the "snow" seen on analog TVs with no signal. Useful for simulating signal loss or creating noise effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Black
member.summary: Solid black color fill.
member.remarks: Generates a completely black frame. Commonly used for fade-outs, blank segments, or as a neutral background.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.White
member.summary: Solid white color fill.
member.remarks: Generates a completely white frame. Used for maximum brightness testing, fade-ins, or as a high-contrast background.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Red
member.summary: Solid red color fill.
member.remarks: Generates a pure red frame. Useful for testing red channel response and color accuracy.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Green
member.summary: Solid green color fill.
member.remarks: Generates a pure green frame. Useful for testing green channel response and color accuracy.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Blue
member.summary: Solid blue color fill.
member.remarks: Generates a pure blue frame. Useful for testing blue channel response and color accuracy.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Checkers1
member.summary: Checkerboard pattern with 1x1 pixel squares.
member.remarks: Finest checkerboard pattern with alternating black and white pixels. Useful for testing display resolution and sharpness.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Checkers2
member.summary: Checkerboard pattern with 2x2 pixel squares.
member.remarks: Medium-fine checkerboard pattern. Good for testing scaling algorithms and pixel accuracy.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Checkers4
member.summary: Checkerboard pattern with 4x4 pixel squares.
member.remarks: Standard checkerboard pattern. Commonly used for testing video compression and transmission quality.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Checkers8
member.summary: Checkerboard pattern with 8x8 pixel squares.
member.remarks: Coarse checkerboard pattern. Useful for basic pattern testing and visual calibration.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Circular
member.summary: Circular pattern with concentric rings.
member.remarks: Generates concentric circles radiating from the center. Useful for testing aspect ratio, display geometry, and radial distortion.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Blink
member.summary: Alternating black and white frames.
member.remarks: Rapidly alternates between black and white frames. Useful for testing frame rate, response time, and temporal processing.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Smpte75
member.summary: SMPTE color bars at 75% intensity.
member.remarks: Similar to standard SMPTE bars but with colors at 75% intensity. Provides a less saturated version for broadcast compliance and preventing over-modulation.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.ZonePlate
member.summary: Zone plate pattern for frequency response testing.
member.remarks: A circular pattern with increasing spatial frequency toward the edges. Used to test resolution limits, aliasing, and frequency response of video systems.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Gamut
member.summary: Color gamut test pattern.
member.remarks: Displays a range of colors to test the full color gamut capabilities of the display or video pipeline. Useful for color space verification.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.ChromaZonePlate
member.summary: Zone plate pattern with chromatic information.
member.remarks: Similar to the standard zone plate but includes color information. Used to test color resolution, chromatic aberration, and color subsampling artifacts.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.SolidColor
member.summary: Solid color fill with configurable color.
member.remarks: Generates a frame filled with a single solid color. The specific color is typically configurable through additional parameters. Useful for color accuracy testing and as a background element.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTransitionType
member.summary: Specifies the type of visual transition effect between video clips.

remarks.para: Video transitions provide smooth visual effects when switching between video clips in a timeline. These transitions are commonly used in video editing to create professional-looking scene changes.

The transitions are organized by categories: - Wipe transitions (1-99): Linear movements that reveal the new clip - Iris transitions (100-199): Shape-based reveals from center or corners - Clock/radial transitions (200-299): Circular and rotational effects - Matrix transitions (300-399): Grid and pattern-based effects - Fade transitions (500+): Opacity-based transitions
Transition codes follow the SMPTE 258M-2004 standard where applicable.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode
member.summary: Specifies the method used for interpolating values between defined points in a 3D space. Each method offers different trade-offs between computational complexity, accuracy, and smoothness.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode.Nearest
member.summary: Uses values from the nearest defined point without any actual interpolation. Fastest method but produces discontinuous results at boundaries between regions. Best used when computational speed is critical and discontinuities are acceptable.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode.Trilinear
member.summary: Interpolates values using all 8 vertices of the surrounding cube. Performs three linear interpolations along each axis, hence "trilinear". Produces continuous results but may show artifacts at sharp transitions. Computational complexity: O(8) - requires 7 linear interpolations.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode.Tetrahedral
member.summary: Interpolates using 4 points forming a tetrahedron within the cube. Divides the cube into 5-6 tetrahedra and selects the appropriate one. Provides better handling of diagonal gradients compared to trilinear. Computational complexity: O(4) - requires 3 linear interpolations.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode.Pyramid
member.summary: Interpolates using 5 points forming a pyramid within the cube. Combines aspects of tetrahedral and trilinear methods. Good balance between accuracy and computational cost. Computational complexity: O(5) - requires 4 linear interpolations.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode.Prism
member.summary: Interpolates using 6 points forming a triangular prism within the cube. Useful for datasets with strong directional bias. Better preservation of sharp features along one primary axis. Computational complexity: O(6) - requires 5 linear interpolations.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX
member.summary: Represents detailed information about a video frame, including its dimensions, pixel format, stride, and frame rate. This class is used within the MediaBlocks framework to describe the characteristics of video data.
member.remarks: This information is crucial for configuring video processing blocks, encoders, and renderers, ensuring that video data is handled correctly throughout the pipeline. The property is automatically calculated for common RGB/RGBA formats if not explicitly set.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX._stride
member.summary: The internal backing field for the property.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Width
member.summary: Gets or sets the width of the video frame in pixels.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Height
member.summary: Gets or sets the height of the video frame in pixels.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the pixel format of the video frame.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Stride
member.summary: Gets or sets the stride (or pitch) of the video frame in bytes. This is the number of bytes required to store one row of pixels. If not explicitly set, it will be calculated automatically for common RGB/RGBA formats based on and .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.PlaneCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of planes in the video format. Optional. For planar formats (e.g., I420, NV12), this would be 2 or 3. For packed formats (e.g., RGB, YUY2), it's typically 1.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Strides
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of strides for each plane in a planar video format. Optional.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Offsets
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of offsets for each plane in a planar video format. Optional.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.FrameRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate of the video stream.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX
member.summary: Represents a single video frame within the VisioForge MediaBlocks framework. This class extends to include the actual pixel data, timestamp, and duration.
member.remarks: VideoFrameX is designed for efficient handling of video frames in a pipeline, supporting direct memory access for performance. It provides methods for memory allocation, deallocation, data copying, and conversion to other frame types. Proper memory management using and is crucial to prevent memory leaks.

member.summary: Gets or sets the total size of the video data buffer in bytes.

member.summary: Gets or sets the presentation timestamp of the video frame.

member.summary: Gets or sets the duration of the video frame.

member.summary: Gets or sets the GStreamer caps string that describes the media format of this frame.
